newsitem.title: USA: Chevron has new South China Sea find.
newsitem.headline: Chevron has new South China Sea find.

text.p: Chevron Corp said Thursday the CACT Operators Group has made a new crude oil discovery in the Huizhou area in tract 16/08 in the Pearl River Mouth Basin of the South China Sea.
Chevron, Texaco Inc and Agip SpA each have a 16-2/3 percent interest in the group, while the China National Offshore Oil Corp holds the remaining 51 percent.

The discovery well, designated Huizhou (HZ) 32-5-1, encountered multiple oil-bearing sands and tested three zones, two of which were successful and which yielded crude oil at a combined rate of 6,900 barrels per day, it said.
Richard Matzke, president of Chevron Overseas Petroleum Inc, noted the "Huizhou 32-5-1 (previously named HZ/26-1 SE-1) represents the latest in a series of crude oil discoveries which began in 1985."
The CACT consortium's total production from four fields in the Pearl River Delta reached record levels of 120,000 barrels per day, Matzke said.

He pointed out the new discovery was drilled in the same exploration and producing area as the Huizhou 32-2 and 32-3 oil fields brought onto production last year, and lies only 2.3 miles (3.7 kilometers) southeast of the Huizhou 26-1 oil field, which was brought onto production in 1991 and serves as a gathering point for the area's oil fields.
He said further appraisal of the HZ/32-5-1 discovery will be conducted in early 1997, following the interpretation of a recently acquired 3-D seismic survey.

"The production could be tied to the Huizhou 26-1 platform using a number of development possibilities if the appraisals determine that this new discovery is of a commercial nature," Matzke said. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
